thread:
maria: Heads up, we started getting SAML ACS failures after the IdP cert rotation for a small set of tenants. Error shows 'invalid character in NameID'. Affected accounts seem to have non-ascii emails (e.g. josé@acme.com). Anyone seen encoding issues like this?
aj: Share the ACS error + a redacted SAML payload if possible.
maria: ACS log: `saml/acs: processing error: invalid NameID characters (NameID='josé@acme.com')`
Redacted assertion snippet:
```
<NameID Format="urn:oasis:names:tc:SAML:1.1:nameid-format:emailAddress">josé@acme.com</NameID>
```
devon: That smells like an XML parsing/byte -> rune mishandling. Which saml SP library/version is currently in prod?
maria: Prod running sp-auth v2.3.1. We have v2.4.0 in staging. I recall a note about unicode fixes in v2.4.
samir: Confirmed: v2.4.0 switched to an XML parser config that preserves UTF-8 properly and removed a legacy ascii-normalisation step that could mangle multibyte NameID values. BUT also noticed we rolled a cookie header sanitizer in front of ACS last month to enforce cookie prefixing. The sanitizer does regex replaces and it isn't utf8-safe; it can truncate bytes in headers which, for multipart/form-data POSTs, can shift boundary offsets and lead to truncated base64 XML -> parser sees invalid chars. Repro is easy:
```
curl -s -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}\n' -X POST https://acs.redwood.ai/sso/saml/acs \
  -F "SAMLResponse=@bad-assertion.b64" \
  -H "Cookie: session=aaa; user=josé; locale=es-ES"
```
maria: We have a customer repro matching that curl. So two likely causes: older sp lib (2.3.1) not handling unicode NameIDs, and sanitizer corrupting POST body.
aj: Proposed immediate actions: 1) roll back cookie sanitizer change to last utf8-safe version on edge-proxy, 2) promote sp-auth v2.4.0 from staging to canary then prod, 3) alert affected tenants with temporary IdP mapping advice (use NameID in ascii-safe attribute). I'll take 1 and 2.
samir: I'll scan KMS logs but assertions are encrypted with our SP key (local), so KMS not implicated for these failures. I'll open an incident follow-up and a short postmortem if rollback needed.
deploy-bot: system: rolled back cookie-sanitizer on edge-proxy at 2024-06-18T15:02:00Z per rollback request #9876.
maria: After rollback and sp-auth promotion to canary, auths for the impacted tenants look healthy in the last 5 minutes. I'll draft a brief postmortem outlining root cause (utf8-unsafe cookie rewrite + legacy ascii coercion in sp-auth) and recommend unit tests for multibyte cookies and NameID values. Closing for now, will follow up with PR links. :thumbsup:
